about.title: Merced Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Merced recorded 3 traffic deaths in 2025, alongside 246 injury collisions across the city. Each of those numbers stands for a household that changed overnight. If yours is one of them, or if you lost a loved one to another kind of negligence here, a wrongful death claim is the civil path California gives surviving family members. It runs separately from any criminal case the Merced County District Attorney may pursue, and it does not depend on a conviction. The law puts a spouse or domestic partner and children first in line to file; certain dependents and heirs may qualify when there is no one in that first group. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks sharply when a city, county, or state agency is involved. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm; the attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out your family's position before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but a much shorter window applies when a government entity is involved. Getting connected quickly protects those dates.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, and our connection service costs nothing. Your family can focus on each other rather than on legal bills.

items.question: My loved one was killed in a crash on G Street in Merced. Does a criminal charge against the driver replace a civil claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death case is a civil action that runs on its own track, apart from whatever the Merced County District Attorney decides to do. It uses a lower standard of proof and focuses on your family's losses rather than punishment. You can pursue it whether or not criminal charges are filed.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children have the first right to file. If there is no one in that group, certain dependents or heirs may be able to step in. Because the rules are specific, an attorney will confirm exactly who in your family qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to act, and what if a public agency is involved?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death. If a city, county, or state agency may share responsibility, the timeline is considerably shorter and starts with an administrative claim. Reaching out early gives an attorney room to preserve evidence and meet every deadline.
